verdict_reason: New product paths are profiled, but the species path reference-data calls escapes latency and faults, and the interface label is now stale.

todos.issue: The mdm latency and fault paths match the request URI exactly, so /mdm/trade/product/commodities/{code}/species, which trade-imports-reference-data calls in production (MdmClient.java:50, ExternalCall get-commodity-species), is never delayed or faulted: a --perf stack answers it at zero latency and resilience runs cannot fail it, so the species lookup's timeout and fallback go untested against the stub. README.md:82 records the gap instead of closing it.
todos.fix: Must: every MDM path reference-data calls, the templated species path included, is delayed by the mdm latency profile and can carry an mdm fault. One way: let StubLatencies.forPath and StubFaults match a path template (for example /mdm/trade/product/commodities/*/species) and list it here, then drop the README sentence that excuses it.

todos.issue: The mdm interface-name still reads 'countries and border control posts' although this PR adds the product search and commodities paths to the same integration; /latency-profiles reports this label, so it now understates what the profile covers.
todos.fix: Must: the mdm interface-name names every MDM interface the profile's paths cover. One way: 'MDM reference data through APIM: countries, border control posts and products'.

todos.issue: The mdm block this PR edits carries a ruling id in its service-level-source ('Interim (c-011 default)'), as does trade-token at line 111; the house rules ban ruling ids in code and config the repo ships.
todos.fix: Must: no ruling ids in application.yml values. One way: 'Interim default: §9.5 MDM through APIM latency is TBC', with the ruling recorded in docs/ if it is needed.
